title: Lakefront and river-parish playing spots, Lacroix's band and McCombs
summary: Recalls playing near the 17th Street Canal, down the river at Boothville, with Lacroix and others, and how George McCombs took over Dumaine's band, with Oliver Alcorn.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: The 17th Street Canal Every night I'd get me a... Well they call it the 17th Street Canal where they say. Well the 17th Street Canal was run into it. Yeah, where it goes right into the lake. That's where it sits, right off the lake. Canal right there by the 17th Street Canal. That's Brooklyn. Right on the corner. I think that's the line for Jefferson Parish too. That's what I was trying to get together. Right on the line of Jefferson Parish.
That used to play out the Beerus too.
Used to play in the Beerus too. Oh yeah. Arnensboro, the Lothel Street.

Down the Beerus? Down the river. That is it. Right by Hatch. Boywoods. Used to play way down in the mountain. Boywood is that place where you have to get the boat to go.
